sentences.text:
The order of ld. Trial court is reproduced herein below:
"An application u/s 245 (2) Cr.P.C. has been filed on behalf of accused for seeking discharge from the present matter stating that there is nothing on record to proceed further as neither the Khasra number nor plot number or gali number are mentioned in the entire charge sheet.

Arguments addressed on the abovesaid application by Ld. APP stating that after framing of charge u/s. 240 Cr.P.C., the accused cannot be discharged and hence, the present application is not maintainable.
Submission heard.
Record perused.

In the present matter, perusal of record reveals that on 04.07.2014, the accused was charged for alleged commission of offence u/s. 448 IPC and since, the charge has already been framed and the said order has not been challanged by the accused till date, therefore, there is no question of discharge of accused by invoking the provision of Section 245 Cr.P.C..
Hence, the application is dismissed.
Witnesses mentioned at serial no. 1 and 2 be summoned for PE on 12.12.2017.

Copy of order be given dasti to the counsel for accused as prayed for."
3.
The facts necessary for disposal of petition are that the petitioner is facing trial for offence punishable under Section 448 IPC filed by the complainant.
The FIR was registered on the allegation that the complainant owns a plot no. 0-45, measuring 125 Sq. Yds.

In Khasra no. 482/22,
Krishna Vihar, Delhi which was purchased by his father in 1999 from one Ram Singh and since purchase it was in possession of complainant.
However, on 25.08.2012 complainant came to know that petitioner has trespassed at the plot of complainant and forcefully taken possession of the same ousting the complainant.
Prior to that on 16.08.2012 also petitioner had made a similar attempt but it was compromised and a civil suit was also pending between same parties with respect to said plot.

On the basis of this complaint, after investigation, police filed the charge sheet for offence under Section 448 IPC.
4.
It is stated in the revision petition that complainant has raised his claim on the basis of forge documents.
Therefore, petitioner had filed quashing petition before Hon'ble High Court of Delhi which was dismissed as withdrawn.
It is also stated that petitioner has also filed a complaint under Section 200 Cr.P.C. along with application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. in which FIR has been directed to be registered.
Therefore, since it has been prima facie shown that the documents of complainant has been forged, the entire case of complainant and prosecution is false.
Hence, the order dated 18.07.2017 needs to be set aside and petitioner be discharged.

sentences.text: As recorded above, the charge against petitioner was already framed before moving application under Section 245 (2) CrP.C.
Therefore, ld. MM had no power to turn the wheel back to a stage of hearing on charge, the application was rightly dismissed as it was not maintainable.
Hence, there is no illegality in order of ld. Trial Court.

6. This petition, however, appears to be an attempt to avoid the trial after framing of charge only because in a separate complaint filed by the petitioner, this Court has passed orders under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. for the investigation of offences under SC/ST Act.
Otherwise there is no justification of waiting for six years before filing the present petition.
7. Hence, the petition which is not only time barred but also devoid of any merits, is dismissed.
8. File be consigned to record room.
A copy of this judgment be be sent to ld. Trial Court.
